title: Orbit
description: Connecting evidence, specialist jobs, drafting and review in a content operation, with an inspectable boundary between preparing work and publishing it.
techStack: Shell, Python, Node.js, JSON job definitions, Local models
status: Public showcase replacement prepared locally; deployment pending

blocks.heading: The operation is the product
blocks.body: Orbit coordinates jobs with different responsibilities: planning, analytics, research, optimisation, writing and review. The difficult part is keeping evidence, account identity and the state of the work attached as it passes between them. A collection of prompts does not establish that a useful result reached the end.

blocks.heading: The old demo showed the wrong evidence
blocks.what: The public control room generated its own activity, tool calls, publication totals and estimated spend. It could look like a functioning operation without showing any real execution evidence.
blocks.why: It illustrated a tidy pipeline rather than the current implementation. The scheduler is a script, and the lean content path is review-only. A fixed fleet count and animated publishing board obscured those distinctions.
blocks.fix: The replacement is an interactive source walkthrough with full, lean-content and research modes. Stage details show inputs, outputs, boundaries and retained source excerpts. It is labelled as a dated implementation snapshot, not a live run.

blocks.heading: Separate the modes
blocks.context: Research, drafting and a full orchestration cycle do not need the same chain of work.

options.label: One pipeline for every task
options.detail: A simple explanation that hides differences in responsibility and cost.

options.label: Show the distinct code paths
options.detail: The full path coordinates planning and enrichment. Lean content writes and reviews. Research updates context without running the writing stages.

blocks.outcome: The walkthrough reflects the selected orchestration paths without claiming every job runs on every cycle. Model-backed jobs and deterministic scripts are distinct.

blocks.heading: A passing score is not publishing authority
blocks.body: The editor’s current instruction is human review only and prohibits creating, scheduling or publishing posts through the connected service. The scheduler source defaults to review-only unless explicitly enabled. Dedicated account pipelines own publishing. Those source boundaries do not prove the current production configuration, which the public walkthrough does not read.

blocks.heading: Keep a place for failed work
blocks.body: The full pipeline records completed and failed jobs in a checkpoint. Resume can skip completed work. Job tiers influence failure handling, so the case study does not claim that every failed dependency always stops downstream work. A later recorded execution should preserve the holds and failures as well as the successful outputs.

blocks.heading: An explanation you can verify
blocks.gave: A constantly moving board with impressive-looking numbers.
blocks.got: A finite, inspectable source snapshot with no model request on a visitor’s click. Runtime claims need a separate reviewed execution record.

blocks.heading: What this audit used
blocks.body: The replacement was checked against the local orchestrator.sh, scheduler configuration and scripts, and research-contract implementation on 20 November 2026. That working tree contains unreleased changes. The public demo replacement is prepared separately from the production runtime; no schedules, agents or publishing permissions were changed.

blocks.heading: Enforce the interface policy without running the operation
blocks.body: Local bdf3de9 adds normal scoped lint and test commands for showcase/dashboard source. A contextual stage-button arrow now uses the existing Lucide renderer; dashboard navigation uses named official Lucide nodes. The pipeline topology connector, sparklines and Orbit brand initial remain reviewed diagram/data/brand content. Sixteen source/syntax/mock-DOM checks include the eleven canonical regressions, with audit zero. Pure dashboard navigation was tested in isolation; no dashboard service, private state, credentials, job trigger or operational API was opened. This does not certify runtime behaviour or replace a recorded execution.
